title: In 322 Allen Neuropixels probes of mouse visual cortex, the unipolar LFP alpha-beta/gamma crossover was in layer 5, 220 µm below CCF layer 4; bipolar and CSD signals did not show the gradient
abstract: Question: Mendoza-Halliday et al. (2024) proposed that the depth where relative alpha-beta and gamma LFP power cross marks cortical layer 4. In mouse, they assigned layers from this pattern itself. We tested the crossover against anatomical layers. Approach: We used 322 Neuropixels probes in visual cortex of 57 mice (Allen Brain Observatory Visual Coding). We read grey-screen and flash-block LFP by HTTP byte ranges. We labelled each channel with its CCFv3 layer and found the flash CSD early sink. A FLIP-like search found the pattern and its crossover in unipolar, common-average, bipolar and CSD-domain signals. Intervals are session-bootstrap 95% intervals. Results: The pattern occurred in 81% of probes (unipolar) and 77% (common average), but in 11% (bipolar) and 4% (CSD), against 2% for shuffled depth order. The unipolar crossover was a median 218 µm (205-237) below the CCF layer-4 centre. It was in layer 5 in 149 of 170 probes and inside layer 4 in 2.4%. Common-average crossovers were 310 µm deeper than layer 4. An atlas rule without LFP predicted layer-4 depth with a 20 µm median error; a calibrated crossover gave 54 µm. The crossover tracked layer-4 depth only through cortical thickness. The flash CSD early sink was 90 µm above the layer-4 centre and about 300 µm above the crossover. Flash stimulation and running moved the crossover by only 5 and 20 µm. Limitation: CCF layers come from track registration, not local histology, and the CSD sink and CCF layer 4 disagree by about 90 µm. Our algorithm is not the published FLIP code. The result applies to head-fixed mouse visual cortex only.

display.caption: Left: unipolar crossover depth against CCF layer-4 centre depth (bars show the layer-4 span) for 169 probes, spontaneous block. The dashed line shows equality. Middle: absolute error against the CCF layer-4 centre for the crossover, the leave-one-session-out calibrated crossover, two atlas rules that use no LFP, and the flash CSD early sink. Right: CCF layer at the crossover and at the CSD sink.

Mean relative alpha-beta (10-19 Hz, blue) and gamma (75-150 Hz, orange) power by depth, aligned to the CCF layer-4 centre (0; grey band shows a typical layer-4 span), for four signal derivations and two conditions (272 probes). Shading: 95% session-bootstrap interval.

Fraction of probes with the primate-type pattern (alpha-beta increases and gamma decreases with depth), by derivation and condition. Whiskers: 95% session-bootstrap interval. Dotted lines: rate after shuffling the depth order of sites.

citations.reason: Source of the spectrolaminar motif and the FLIP method; we test its layer-4 crossover claim against anatomy in the same mouse data set.
Allen Brain Observatory Visual Coding Neuropixels data set (LFP, channel CCF coordinates, stimulus tables).
Allen CCFv3 annotation used for channel layer labels.
Preprint that questions whether the crossover identifies layer 4; our mouse result agrees with this concern.
Rebuttal preprint that defends the motif with histology in primates.
